title: More Than a Thank-You: The Unexpected Gains of Volunteering
title_zh: 不只是感谢：志愿服务的意外收获
intro_zh: 本文约930词（目标900词左右），通过作者在养老院做志愿者的真实经历，讲述服务他人如何反过来给志愿者带来心理、社交和技能上的成长。含6个重点词汇，难度适中，适合CET-4阶段阅读。

paragraphs.en: Two years ago, I joined a volunteer program at a local nursing home. Honestly, my first reason was not pure kindness. I needed some experience for my resume, and I thought a certificate would look good in future job interviews. I expected a few simple tasks such as answering phones or cleaning tables, and then a quick exit. But an unexpected chat changed everything. This experience gave me far more than a line on my resume. It showed me the hidden value of spending time with people who are often forgotten. I learned that a few hours of attention can mean the world to someone who feels invisible.
paragraphs.zh: 两年前，我报名参加了当地一家养老院的志愿活动。老实说，我的最初动机并非纯粹的善意。我需要一些简历上的经历。我原以为只是做些接电话、擦桌子的简单任务，然后很快结束。但一次意外的交谈改变了一切。这段经历给我的远不止简历上的一行字。它让我看到了花时间陪伴那些常被遗忘的人所蕴含的隐秘价值。我明白了，几小时的关注对某个感到自己隐形的人来说，可能意味着整个世界。

paragraphs.en: My first regular task was to sit with an elderly woman named Margaret. For weeks we only talked about the weather or the meals. Then one afternoon she began to tell stories about her youth. She described how she met her husband in a small library, and how she worked as a nurse during a difficult time. She also showed me old black-and-white photos, pointing at each person with a smile. I slowly realized that my presence was more than a polite duty. It offered true companionship. In return, her stories became a window into a different world. I started to feel a sense of well-being that surprised me. It was not the excitement of a new activity, but a warm, steady feeling inside.
paragraphs.zh: 我的第一项常规任务是陪伴一位名叫玛格丽特的老太太。起初几周，我们只聊天气和饭菜。后来有一天下午，她开始讲述她年轻时的故事。她描述了她在小图书馆里结识丈夫的过程，以及她在艰难时期当护士的经历。她还给我看了泛黄的黑白照片，笑着指认每一个人。我慢慢意识到，我的出现不仅仅是一种礼貌的职责。它带来了真正的陪伴。作为回报，她的故事成了通往另一个世界的窗口。我开始感到一种令我惊讶的幸福感。那并非参与新活动的兴奋，而是一种温暖、平稳的内心感受。

paragraphs.en: Scientists have found that volunteering can improve mental health in measurable ways. A 2020 study from the University of Exeter reported that people who volunteered regularly felt less stressed and more hopeful. They also showed lower levels of depression. The effect was strongest among those who gave at least two hours each week. Interestingly, the researchers compared the benefit to the effect of regular exercise. Why does this happen? One reason is that helping others reduces our focus on ourselves. It builds empathy, the ability to feel another person's emotions. This connection makes our own problems look smaller and more manageable. Over time, this habit can shape a more positive and balanced mind.
paragraphs.zh: 科学家发现，志愿服务能以可衡量的方式改善心理健康。埃克塞特大学2020年的一项研究报告称，经常做志愿者的人压力更小、更有希望，抑郁水平也更低。这种效应在每周至少投入两小时的人身上最为明显。有趣的是，研究人员将这种益处与定期锻炼的效果进行了比较。为什么会这样？一个原因是，帮助他人会减少我们对自身的关注。它培养同理心——即感受他人情绪的能力。这种联结让我们自己的问题看起来更小、更易应付。久而久之，这种习惯能塑造更积极、更平衡的心态。

paragraphs.en: Volunteering also opens the door to new relationships. At the nursing home, I met people from completely different backgrounds: a retired teacher, a former factory worker, and a soldier. At first, we seemed to have nothing in common. But over time, shared moments of laughter and patience created real bonds. One retired teacher, Mr. Lin, taught me how to play Chinese chess and told me about his years in a remote village. These connections reduced my loneliness and widened my social circle. For young people, this is especially important. Modern life can feel isolated even when we are online all day. Talking face to face with others gives us a form of support that no text message can replace.
paragraphs.zh: 志愿服务还打开了结识新朋友的大门。在养老院，我遇到了背景完全不同的人：一位退休教师、一位前工厂工人和一位士兵。起初，我们似乎毫无共同点。但随着时间的推移，共同的笑声和耐心营造了真正的纽带。其中一位退休教师林先生教我下中国象棋，还给我讲他在偏远乡村度过的岁月。这些联系减轻了我的孤独感，拓宽了我的社交圈。对年轻人来说，这尤为重要。现代生活即使我们整天在线，也可能让人感到孤立。与他人面对面交谈给予我们的支持，是任何短信都无法替代的。

paragraphs.en: Besides emotional gains, I learned practical skills that were not taught in college. I had to plan activities for the elderly, solve small problems like slow wheelchairs, and communicate patiently with people who had hearing loss. These tasks taught me flexibility and responsibility. For example, I once organized a simple music game that required careful timing and clear instructions. I also discovered that a simple gesture such as holding a hand or offering a smile can calm someone down. This training in human interaction has been useful in my part-time job and in my studies. It made me a better listener and a quicker thinker. Even more, I learned to notice small needs and act without being asked.
paragraphs.zh: 除了情感上的收获，我还学到了大学里没有教过的实用技能。我必须为老人策划活动、解决像轮椅缓慢这类小问题，还要耐心地与有听力障碍的人沟通。这些任务教会了我灵活应变和承担责任。例如，我曾组织过一场简单的音乐游戏，需要精准的时机和清晰的指令。我还发现，握住一只手或送上微笑这样简单的举动就能让人平静下来。这种人际互动的训练在我的兼职工作和学习中都有用。它让我成为更好的倾听者和更敏捷的思考者。更重要的是，我学会了留意细微的需求，并主动行动。

paragraphs.en: Perhaps the greatest change was in my outlook. Before volunteering, I often complained about busy schedules and small failures. Seeing how Margaret faced her own health problems with courage gave me a new perspective. It also filled me with appreciation for the ordinary parts of my life. I began to notice the good food on my table, the freedom to walk, and the friends who cared for me. One day, Margaret said that my smile reminded her of her grandson who lived far away. That simple remark made me realize how much a small act of kindness can mean. These feelings did not come from trying to be positive. They came naturally from comparing my situation with those who faced harder struggles.
paragraphs.zh: 也许最大的改变在于我的心态。做志愿者之前，我常抱怨忙碌的日程和小小的失败。看到玛格丽特如何勇敢地面对自己的健康问题，让我获得了新的视角。它也让我的内心充满对日常生活的感激。我开始注意到桌上可口的饭菜、行走的自由以及关心我的朋友。有一天，玛格丽特说我的笑容让她想起远方的孙子。这句简单的话让我意识到，一个小小的善意举动有多大的意义。这些感受并不是靠努力让自己积极得来的。它们自然而然地产生于将自己与那些遭遇更艰难困境的人相比。

paragraphs.en: Of course, these benefits do not appear by accident. They require a sincere commitment. Volunteers who show up only for a resume might leave quickly when the work gets boring. But if you stay and open your heart, you will find a deep sense of fulfillment. Once, our group organized a small birthday party for Margaret. She laughed and sang with us, and her joy was priceless. That moment showed me that fulfillment is not the loud happiness of receiving a prize. Rather, it is a quiet inner peace that comes from knowing you made someone else's day a little brighter. That feeling stays with you long after the volunteer shift ends.
paragraphs.zh: 当然，这些好处不会凭空出现。它们需要真诚的投入。那些只为简历而来的人，可能在工作变得枯燥时很快离开。但如果你留下并敞开心扉，你就会找到深深的满足感。有一次，我们小组为玛格丽特办了一个小型生日会。她和我们一起笑、一起唱歌，她的快乐是无价的。那一刻让我明白，满足感并不是获奖时那种喧闹的快乐。相反，它是一种安静的内心平静，源于你知道自己让别人的一天变得更明亮了一些。这种感觉在志愿工作结束后仍会伴随你很久。

paragraphs.en: In conclusion, volunteering is not a one-way street. While we give time and energy, we gain far more in return. The benefits range from better mental health to stronger social ties and practical skills. More importantly, it changes how we see ourselves and the world. I strongly encourage every college student to try at least one volunteer activity. It might start as a duty, but it will end as a gift. When you help others, you also help yourself — and that is the hidden reward that makes it all worthwhile. So do not hesitate. Find a cause you care about and give it a try. You will be surprised by what you receive in the process.
paragraphs.zh: 总之，志愿服务不是单向的付出。我们付出时间和精力，换回的却要多得多。这些好处从更好的心理健康到更强的社交联系和实用技能，不一而足。更重要的是，它改变了我们看待自己和世界的方式。我强烈建议每位大学生至少尝试一次志愿活动。它可能始于一份责任，但最终会化为一份礼物。当你帮助别人时，你也在帮助自己——这就是让一切值得的隐藏回报。所以，别犹豫。找一个你关心的事业，试一试。你会对自己在这个过程中获得的东西感到惊讶。

questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Volunteering brings unexpected benefits to the volunteer themselves.
Volunteering is mainly for improving your resume.
Elderly people need more care in nursing homes.
questions.explain: 文章通过作者在养老院做志愿者的经历，重点论述了志愿服务给志愿者本人带来的心理、社交和技能上的意外收获。因此选A。B只是作者最初的动机，不是主旨；C是文中一个细节；D与文章观点相反。

questions.q: According to the 2020 study from the University of Exeter, which group showed the strongest positive effects of volunteering?
options: People who volunteered once a month.
People who volunteered for a whole day every month.
People who volunteered at least two hours a week.
People who volunteered only during holidays.
questions.explain: 文中明确提到'The effect was strongest among those who gave at least two hours each week.'（每周至少投入两小时的人效果最强），因此选C。其他选项均未提及。

questions.q: What can be inferred about the author's feeling after talking with Margaret?
options: The author felt bored and wanted to leave.
The author felt sorry for Margaret's hard life.
The author felt a sense of connection and warmth.
The author felt proud of his own achievements.
questions.explain: 作者说陪伴Margaret时感到一种'温暖、平稳的内心感受'，并产生了幸福感，因此可推断出作者感到一种联结和温暖。A、B、D在文中没有依据。

questions.q: The word 'fulfillment' in Paragraph 7 most probably means ______.
options: a feeling of loneliness and sadness
a feeling of satisfaction and purpose
a feeling of tiredness and stress
a feeling of anger and disappointment
questions.explain: 'fulfillment'出现在第七段，结合'quiet inner peace'和'knowing you made someone else's day a little brighter'可知它指一种满足感和意义感，因此选B。A、C、D都不符合上下文。
